name: IRONCLAD DRIFT: Shelf Freerun Combat Circuit
description: A savage hybrid of freerunning and close-quarters combat, Ironclad Drift pits augmented athletes against each other across collapsing Shelf infrastructure — broken elevated rail lines, flooded sub-basements, and active industrial corridors — where the terrain itself is as lethal as any opponent. Founded by a loose syndicate of former chrome-couriers and disgraced APEX washouts known only as the Driftline Compact, the circuit has no referee, no medical staff on site, and no ruleset beyond a single posted maxim: 'reach the mark or don't come back.' Injuries are common, deaths average three to five per seasonal bracket, and the unofficial feed draws hundreds of thousands of Tier 1 and Tier 2 viewers who wager in Φ scrip and salvage credit on who finishes standing.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 investigative journalist embeds with a Drift crew to expose the Driftline Compact's suspected ties to a chrome-parts black market — only to discover the syndicate is being quietly funded by a Tier 4 corponation executive who bets heavily and fixes outcomes through sabotaged augmentation components.

A former APEX Drift-class athlete, stripped of their corporate sponsorship after a failed doping tribunal, enters the Ironclad circuit under a false identity to earn enough Φ to pay for a younger sibling's geneware treatment — and finds themselves climbing the brackets toward a final against someone they once trained alongside.

The Meridian Civic Authority's chrome-crimes division receives an anonymous tip that a next-generation military-grade limb prototype — stolen from a HelixCorp R&D facility — is being field-tested by a Drift competitor mid-circuit, and sends an undercover operative to retrieve it before the corporation sends its own extraction team.
